title: Reveries V2 cryptographic signature (RVR-009)
description: An immutable signature over a fact record or a ledger manifest. Signatures are a separate record type on purpose: the semantic IDs of reverie, transition, correction, resolution, and redaction records are content hashes of causal fields only, so a signature must never enter one of those payloads or key rotation would change a decision ID. The record therefore carries its own sg: identity derived from its own content and references its target by ID.

id.description: sg: plus the full repository-format object ID derived from this record's own canonical content, including the signature bytes.

domain.description: Domain separator inside the signed payload, so a record signature can never replay as a checkpoint signature. Only these two values are valid; a self-chosen domain would assert a scope this protocol never agreed to.

role.description: Who is attesting. The role is inside the signed payload, so it cannot be swapped after signing.

target.description: The signed record ID, or the reserved ledger-manifest for a checkpoint signature. The reserved target is reachable only under the manifest domain.

subject.description: The annotated object this signature is attached to, or the ledger checkpoint commit.

signer.description: The stable attesting identity. This survives key rotation, unlike key_id.

key_id.description: The key material identity, for example an SSH or public-key fingerprint. This is the field that rotates.

algorithm.description: The signature algorithm name, for example ed25519 or ssh-ed25519.

signature.description: The signature over the canonical signed payload, base64 encoded. Opaque bytes; only the record size budget applies.

content_id.description: Repository object ID of the target's exact canonical bytes: the record's canonical line without its trailing LF, or ledgerManifestPayload for a checkpoint. Binding a hash rather than the bytes keeps the signed payload O(1) and works for both SHA-1 and SHA-256 repositories.

author_email.description: Git email of whoever ran the helper. Separate from signer on purpose, so a shared runner does not masquerade as the attesting identity.

signatureTarget.description: Every ID-bearing fact may be attested, including a redaction: redactions are never supersession heads, but a reviewer may still attest that one was deliberate. The reserved ledger-manifest target is allowed by shape here; the domain pairing is enforced by the protocol, which rejects a record-domain signature naming ledger-manifest.
